title: Looping Over Containers
summary: Use the **range-based for loop**, `for (const auto& x : v)`, whenever you need each element. Use an index loop when you need the position too. Remember that `v.size()` is **unsigned**.
ideas:
1. Print a vector in reverse, safely.
2. Write `std::vector<int> evensOnly(const std::vector<int>& v)`.
3. Find the second-largest element in a single pass.

cards.q: What is the best loop variable for reading strings out of a vector?
cards.a:
`const auto&`

`const auto&` avoids copying each string and stops the loop changing them. Plain `auto` or `std::string` copies every element.

cards.q: Why does `for (std::size_t i{ n - 1 }; i >= 0; --i)` never stop?
cards.a:
An unsigned value is always at least 0, and going below 0 wraps round to a huge number

`i >= 0` is always true for an unsigned type. When `i` is 0, `--i` wraps round to the largest value, and the loop goes on.

cards.q: A loop `for (auto x : v) { x *= 2; }` leaves `v` unchanged. Why?
cards.a:
`auto x` is a copy of each element

`auto x` copies each element, so the copy is doubled. Use `auto& x` to change the elements themselves.

cards.q: Why is calling `push_back` inside a range-based loop over the same vector dangerous?
cards.a:
The vector may reallocate, leaving the loop on freed memory

When the capacity runs out, `push_back` moves the elements to new memory, and the loop's hidden iterators then point at freed memory.
